asIs.html:
Demand to Profit · FP&A Commercial · Stages 1-9 of the Commercial FP&A E2E (simplified v3) and CAPEX planning · LT feedback applied 15 Oct 2026

FP&A Commercial As-Is Process Map

From Brand Manager revenue assumptions to the signed-off P&L and its control attestation: revenue, manpower, non-manpower and CAPEX planning, P&L consolidation and PMR submission with CMR validation, the planning deck, pre-close analysis, monthly revenue and cost reporting, the mid-month forecast and the FCF controls in FAST+. Pain points and activity types reflect the updated As-Is map reviewed with FP&A Commercial.

asIs.title: Pain points 55
asIs.html:
Pain points 55

As documented by FP&A Commercial in the E2E v3, the CAPEX planning summary and the updated As-Is feedback, grouped by stage · red ! on the map marks the step; [CHALLENGE] nodes below each stage list them.

Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand10
Data quality & completeness: manual SKU validation against SAP master data creates risk of omissionsRevenue Planning · step 1
Excel template (>15 MB, VBA) degrades and throws formula errors; no version control; corruption would disrupt the cycleRevenue Planning · step 2
Lack of automation: Excel file degrades with excessive formulas; slow and prone to formula errorsRevenue Planning · step 2
No automated version control: manual file backups used as workaroundRevenue Planning · step 2
Key risk: template corruption could disrupt the entire planning cycleRevenue Planning · step 2
Re-actualisation required when resubmission is needed because of long timelines between planning and area r...Revenue Planning · step 3
Re-actualisation required when resubmission is needed because of long timelines between planning and area reviewRevenue Planning · step 3
Manual copy-paste from Excel to PowerPoint for the reporting packageRevenue Planning · step 7
At least three revision cycles before final PMR submissionRevenue Planning · step 7
Delays and idle time from alignment and scenario discussionsRevenue Planning · step 8
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning14
FTE by Brand templates consume disproportionate effortMPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 1
AZ FORCE missing data at actualisation; new cost centres unavailableMPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 5
Data quality: AZ FORCE frequently has missing data during actualisation; newly created cost centres often unavailable for planningMPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 5
AZ FORCE review layout is not user-friendly, so output review is done in ExcelMPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 6
BUD / HR / Finance misalignment delays conclusion; MPC revised when operating profit misses targetMPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 9
Cost template preparation needs copying past cycles and matching actualsNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 1
Template preparation is not straightforward: copying past cycle details, matching against actuals, careful scrutiny and total checksNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 1
Data quality: duplicated data in actuals / planning where multiple lines with the same GL / CC combination were created in previous cyclesNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 1
Duplicated GL / cost centre lines from previous cyclesNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 3
Cost Tool macros fail and need the tool ownerNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 4
Key risk: heavy reliance on the Cost Tool with multiple macro functions; a macro crash needs significant troubleshootingNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 4
Repetitive rework every time changes happenNMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 8
Pending input from the business (primary pain point)CAPEX Planning · step 2
Delays sometimes come from CBP; sometimes CBP inputs directly into the templateCAPEX Planning · step 3
Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation6
Formula / macro errors on a >15-tab model linked to 20-30 files; key-person dependency; market template variationsP&L Planning · step 2
Formula or macro errors on the >15-tab, ~10 MB file linked to 20 to 30 stakeholder files take significant analyst time to root-causeP&L Planning · step 2
Key risk: key-person dependency; the back-up (manager) takes time to learn the file structureP&L Planning · step 2
Minor standardisation variations (e.g. Malaysia BUD combines CVRM and central TA such as Nexium) need manual template adjustmentP&L Planning · step 2
Wrong SCC / royalty ratesP&L Planning · step 3
VBA macro re-run for every input (~1 hour lag, 4-5 iterations)P&L Planning · step 4
Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation6
Key risk: dependency on timely and accurate Embedded Finance inputsPlanning System Submission · step 1
Manual Gross Margin Pay Away calculation and phasing inputPlanning System Submission · step 4
Master data issues at upload (new cost centre missing in PMR)Planning System Submission · step 5 +1
Heavy manual consolidation and reconciliation across Excel files and systemsPlanning System Submission · step 6 +1
30 min - 1 hr PMR-CMR bridge lag per iterationPlanning System Submission · step 12
Frequent rework loops; key-person riskPlanning System Submission · step 14 +1
Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review4
International templates with formula errors or outdated structures; late distributionPlanning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · step 1
Delays typically originate from late distribution of materials from InternationalPlanning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · step 1
Error checking of international templates; format misaligned with the deckPlanning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · step 2
Repeated refresh and copy-paste into PowerPoint every time numbers changePlanning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · step 3
Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis4
SAP data changes frequently and needs close monitoring for alignment with month-end expectationsPre-close Analysis · step 1
Delayed replies from budget owners on variance queries slow the processPre-close Analysis · step 3
Delays when requested correction journals are not booked in timePre-close Analysis · step 3 +1
Key risk: if not done correctly, the reported monthly numbers are inaccurate and may lead to wrong business decisionsPre-close Analysis · step 7
Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting3
Highly manual multi-source consolidation (SAP, CMR, offline file)Revenue Reporting · step 2 +1
Key risk: heavily manual nature creates exposure to undetected human errorRevenue Reporting · step 13 +1
Market-specific granularity limits standardisation scopeRevenue Reporting · step 13
Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast4
Coincides with month-end close peak; actuals change after WD1Mid-Month Forecast (MMF) · step 1
Data quality: actual sales can continue to change after WD1; early template distribution may give mismatched actualsMid-Month Forecast (MMF) · step 1
Sales forecast collection from BUDs is entirely manual; no online platformMid-Month Forecast (MMF) · step 2
Multiple changes and rework in the sales forecast are routineMid-Month Forecast (MMF) · step 2
Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+4
Missing / incomplete / inconsistent evidenceFCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · step 1 +1
Manual evidence compilation at submissionFCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · step 1
Manual OneGRC upload post-approval (workaround); system limitationsFCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · step 12
Impact: missed or late approvals mean the control cannot be evidenced as performed, creating audit / compliance and control-failure exposureFCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · step 12

asIs.title: Key processes · what each one does
asIs.html:
Key processes · what each one does

As described in the Commercial FP&A E2E simplified v3 and the CAPEX planning summary · owner, window and processes in each stage.

#Key processWhat happensOwnerWindowProcesses
1Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and BrandFPAC-01Excel template performance degradation and formula errors; manual SKU validation against SAP risks omissions; manual (re-)actualisation of historicals when resubmission is needed; idle time from alignment and scenario discussions; no automated version control (manual backups). Key risk: template corruption could disrupt the whole planning cycleFP&A Comm (with Brand Managers)Planning cycles (RBU2 March-April, MTP July-August, Phased Budget); atRevenue Planning (FPAC-01.01)
2Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX PlanningFPAC-02MPC: BUD / HR / Finance misalignment delays conclusion; MPC revised when operating profit misses target; FTE-by-Brand templates consume disproportionate effort; AZ FORCE missing data at actualisation and new cost centres unavailable; key risk - subjective FTE by Brand and MPC allocations misstate brand-level investment. NMPC: cost template preparation needs copying past cycles and matching actuals; Cost Tool macro errors need the tool owner; repetitive rework; duplicated GL / cost centre lines from previous cycles; key risk - heavy reliance on Cost Tool macros. CAPEX: pending input from the business (primary pain point); delays sometimes come from CBP, who sometimes input directlyFP&A Comm (with HR, BUD, cost centre owners, Market Finance and Region)Planning cycles; 4+ revision cycles; CFO sign-off (MPC); CAPEX 1-2 days per cycle (RBU2, MTP, PB)MPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) (FPAC-02.01)
NMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) (FPAC-02.02)
CAPEX Planning (FPAC-02.03)
3Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company ConsolidationFPAC-03VBA macro re-run for every input (~1 hour lag); formula / macro errors on a >15-tab file linked to 20-30 files take significant time to root-cause; wrong SCC / royalty rates and incorrect inputs; key-person dependency on the model; market-specific template adjustments (e.g. Malaysia combining CVRM and central TA)FP&A Comm (sign-off CFO and Country President)~1 week sales and ~1 week cost inputs (often parallel); 4-5 consolidatP&L Planning (FPAC-03.01)
4Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR ValidationFPAC-04Late source files or last-minute changes from Embedded Finance; heavy manual consolidation and reconciliation across Excel files and systems; master data issues at upload (e.g. new cost centre missing in PMR); key-person risk and frequent rework loops; bridge processing lagFP&A Comm (sign-off Controlling (Embedded Finance) / CFO)Per planning cycle; 4+ iterations; 30 min - 1 hr PMR-CMR bridge lag pePlanning System Submission (FPAC-04.01)
5Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership ReviewFPAC-05Repeated template refresh and copy-paste into PowerPoint each time numbers change; error checking of international templates; template format misaligned with the deck; international templates with formula errors or outdated structures; late distribution from international. Key risk: incorrect numbers in the deck mislead review and decisionsFP&A Comm (sign-off GM and CFO)RBU2 (March, completing April); MTP (July, completing August); no deckPlanning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) (FPAC-05.01)
6Stage 6: Pre-Close AnalysisFPAC-06Inaccurate raw bookings need multiple corrections before analysis; delayed replies from budget owners on variance queries; SAP data changes frequently; delays when requested correction journals are not booked in time. Key risk: inaccurate reported numbers lead to wrong decisionsFP&A Comm (review CBP and CFO)WD-4 to WD-1 / WD+1 (~4-5 working days); 4+ revision cycles; CFO sign-Pre-close Analysis (FPAC-06.01)
7Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost ReportingFPAC-07Highly manual multi-source consolidation (SAP, CMR, offline file); manual self-pay vs reimbursement split not supported by the system; SAP-to-CMR discrepancies, outdated SCC and royalty rates, outdated uplift values and FX rates; manual file splitting for unsupported markets; 12 files checked manually against CMR; market-specific granularity limits standardisation. Key risk: fully manual nature exposes to undetected errorFP&A CommRevenue: WD-1 to WD+2 (~1 working day); Cost: WD+2 to WD+5 (~1 workingRevenue Reporting (FPAC-07.01)
Cost Reporting (FPAC-07.02)
8Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling ForecastFPAC-08Forecast collection from BUDs is entirely manual (no online platform); routine rework; coincides with month-end close peak workload; actuals can change after WD1 so early templates mismatch; rework when the forecast misses leadership expectations. Key risk: no system submission - all data in Excel, audit and accuracy exposureFP&A Comm (sign-off CFO and CP and GM)WD1 to WD7 (~7 working days), triggered by the Group / International MMid-Month Forecast (MMF) (FPAC-08.01)
9Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+FPAC-09Manual evidence compilation and OneGRC upload after approval; visibility ends at FAST+ approval; risk of missing, incomplete or inconsistent evidence. Impact: missed or late approvals mean the control cannot be evidenced, creating audit / compliance exposureFP&A Comm (requestor) / CFO or nominated delegate (approver)WD1 to WD7 EOD (~7 days); monthly; 14 APAC markets; typically one iterFCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) (FPAC-09.01)

ai.title: AI opportunities 21
ai.html:
AI opportunities 21

Shown as blue nodes on the map · Claude recommendations · hypotheses to validate with FP&A Commercial
Process ImprovementPlanning calendar with agreed cut-offs per market
Key process · Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand · FPAC-01

Fix the revenue planning calendar and cut-offs with the market after the Business Strategy Meetings, reducing idle time between alignment discussions.

AIAI baseline volume per SKU for Brand Managers
Process · Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand · Revenue Planning · FPAC-01.01

A statistical baseline per SKU from the phased actuals is pre-filled for Brand Managers, who adjust it with their assumptions; fewer revision cycles start from a blank template.

DigitalizationOne planning intake for MPC, NMPC and CAPEX
Key process · Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · FPAC-02

One SharePoint / Power Apps intake hub for brand FTE, cost centre and CAPEX inputs with shared reminders and a status view for FP&A and Market Finance.

Process ImprovementBrand-level FTE field in AZ FORCE
Process · Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · MPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · FPAC-02.01

Raise a change request for brand-level FTE input in AZ FORCE, so brand allocation is captured in the planning system instead of a side Excel collection.

AIAI anomaly screening of cost centre inputs
Process · Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · NMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · FPAC-02.02

A model trained on prior cycles and actuals flags unusual cost lines before the FP&A review, focusing the review loop.

DigitalizationCAPEX planning tool with an embedded approval flow
Process · Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · CAPEX Planning · FPAC-02.03

The improvement named in the CAPEX planning summary: one tool for business input, CBP review, CFO approval and the Region submission, replacing template cascades by email.

Process ImprovementReduce the key-person dependency on the master P&L model
Key process · Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation · FPAC-03

Document the model (tab map, inputs vs logic, run steps) and rotate a trained back-up through each cycle.

AIAI-drafted P&L bridge between iterations
Process · Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation · P&L Planning · FPAC-03.01

Copilot drafts the bridge between P&L iterations (what changed by brand and P&L line, and why) for the CFO / CP alignment.

Process ImprovementAgreed input cut-off with Embedded Finance
Key process · Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation · FPAC-04

A fixed cut-off for Embedded Finance files per iteration, with changes after it going to the next iteration.

AutomationOne validation suite for the PMR submission
Process · Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation · Planning System Submission · FPAC-04.01

Conso Check, PMR load, PMR vs Analytics and PMR vs CMR run as one scripted suite per iteration with a single exceptions report.

Process ImprovementDeck-aligned international template released on a fixed date
Key process · Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review · FPAC-05

Agree with International Finance a locked template that matches the deck, released on a fixed date per cycle.

AICopilot draft of the deck narrative
Process · Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review · Planning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · FPAC-05.01

Copilot drafts the key messages per slide from the refreshed numbers for FP&A to edit.

Process ImprovementRoot-cause log of correction requests
Key process · Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis · FPAC-06

Log pre-close correction requests by root cause (wrong cost centre, missing accrual, wrong period) and share a monthly summary with the booking teams, so repeat errors are prevented.

Process ImprovementBring known accruals into the pre-close view
Process · Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis · Pre-close Analysis · FPAC-06.01

Late costs advised informally by Embedded Finance and known accrual lists show as expected postings, so fewer variances need a query.

Process ImprovementStandard revenue and cost output structure across markets
Key process · Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · FPAC-07

Agree a common core structure for the revenue and cost outputs with market-specific add-ons, so scripts and dashboards can be reused.

AutomationPython build of the 37-tab revenue master
Process · Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Revenue Reporting · FPAC-07.01

One scripted run builds the revenue master from SAP and CMR extracts with the reconciliation, rules and checks above.

DigitalizationSAP-CMR reconciliation page on the RLS dashboard
Process · Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Cost Reporting · FPAC-07.02

Show the SAP vs CMR reconciliation and stale FX / uplift values on the cost dashboard, so discrepancies are visible to everyone using it.

Process ImprovementDecouple forecast collection from the month-end peak
Key process · Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast · FPAC-08

Start BUD collection on a flash of prior-month sales and refresh actuals once final, so MMF does not collide with month-end close.

AIAI baseline sales forecast for BUD review
Process · Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast · Mid-Month Forecast (MMF) · FPAC-08.01

A run-rate and seasonality baseline per brand is pre-filled so BUDs forecast the delta, reducing routine rework.

Process ImprovementStandard evidence pack per FSC control
Key process · Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+ · FPAC-09

Define the minimum evidence set for FSC008, FSC009 and FSC011 as a checklist in FAST+ across the 14 markets.

DigitalizationPower BI control status across 14 markets
Process · Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+ · FCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · FPAC-09.01

Submission, approval, delegation and OneGRC upload status by market and control (FSC008, FSC009, FSC011) in one view.

Reduce the key-person dependency on the master P&L modelDocument the model (tab map, inputs vs logic, run steps) and rotate a trained back-up through each cycle.
Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation · Planning System Submission
One validation suite for the PMR submissionConso Check, PMR load, PMR vs Analytics and PMR vs CMR run as one scripted suite per iteration with a single exceptions report.
Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation
Agreed input cut-off with Embedded FinanceA fixed cut-off for Embedded Finance files per iteration, with changes after it going to the next iteration.
Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review · Planning Review Preparation
Copilot draft of the deck narrativeCopilot drafts the key messages per slide from the refreshed numbers for FP&A to edit.
Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review
Deck-aligned international template released on a fixed dateAgree with International Finance a locked template that matches the deck, released on a fixed date per cycle.
Bring known accruals into the pre-close viewLate costs advised informally by Embedded Finance and known accrual lists show as expected postings, so fewer variances need a query.

Root-cause log of correction requestsLog pre-close correction requests by root cause (wrong cost centre, missing accrual, wrong period) and share a monthly summary with the booking teams, so repeat errors are prevented.
Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Revenue Reporting
Python build of the 37-tab revenue masterOne scripted run builds the revenue master from SAP and CMR extracts with the reconciliation, rules and checks above.
Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Cost Reporting
SAP-CMR reconciliation page on the RLS dashboardShow the SAP vs CMR reconciliation and stale FX / uplift values on the cost dashboard, so discrepancies are visible to everyone using it.
Standard revenue and cost output structure across marketsAgree a common core structure for the revenue and cost outputs with market-specific add-ons, so scripts and dashboards can be reused.
Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast · Mid-Month Forecast
AI baseline sales forecast for BUD reviewA run-rate and seasonality baseline per brand is pre-filled so BUDs forecast the delta, reducing routine rework.
Decouple forecast collection from the month-end peakStart BUD collection on a flash of prior-month sales and refresh actuals once final, so MMF does not collide with month-end close.
Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+ · FCF Control on Revenue and P&L
Power BI control status across 14 marketsSubmission, approval, delegation and OneGRC upload status by market and control (FSC008, FSC009, FSC011) in one view.
Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+
Standard evidence pack per FSC controlDefine the minimum evidence set for FSC008, FSC009 and FSC011 as a checklist in FAST+ across the 14 markets.
Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand · Revenue Planning · step 3

Power BI semantic model with scheduled refreshSKU-level actuals from SAP and CMR refresh into one Power BI semantic model that the revenue template reads, alongside the Python step, so the actualisation does not depend on a script run from one laptop.
Power BI semantic model with scheduled refresh

Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand · Revenue Planning · step 6
Copilot Studio agent in TeamsA Brand Manager agent shares the template, answers input questions from the planning guidance, chases late volume and net-price inputs and logs what has been submitted.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · MPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 2

Agent Builder agent (Microsoft 365 Copilot)An agent grounded on the brand allocation keys answers 'which key applies to this brand' for planners and HR, so the form is filled once with the right default.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · MPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning) · step 6
Copilot in Power BICopilot writes the plain-language summary of the AZ FORCE output (movement by brand and cost line vs the last cycle) that FP&A, HR and BUD review in the alignment call.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · NMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 2
Copilot Studio agent in TeamsAn agent sends each cost-centre owner their template link, tracks the status and chases only the owners still open, with the status visible on the tracker.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · NMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning) · step 5

Copilot in Power BI (Q&A)Department heads and the FP&A analyst ask the cost review in natural language (for example 'which cost centres moved most vs last year') and get answers with the underlying GL lines.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · CAPEX Planning · step 2
Power Apps with AI BuilderAI Builder checks each CAPEX request for completeness and classifies the project type and approval route as it is entered, before it reaches the Region.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation · P&L Planning · step 5
Copilot in Power BICopilot drafts the iteration-on-iteration narrative of the P&L view (what moved, why) for the CBP, CFO and BU discussion; the analyst confirms before it is shown.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation · P&L Planning · step 6
Microsoft 365 Copilot in TeamsCopilot recaps the CFO and Country President alignment meeting, lists the agreed changes and sends them as actions to the next iteration.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation · Planning System Submission · step 15
Copilot Studio agentAn agent reads the validation exceptions, groups them by root cause, proposes the fix owner and drafts the message to Embedded Finance or the market for the rework.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review · Planning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation) · step 3
Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPointCopilot drafts the slide narrative from the refreshed CMR numbers so the deck text and AZcreate figures start from one draft; the FP&A owner edits.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis · Pre-close Analysis · step 2
Copilot in Power BICopilot explains each variance line in plain language from the SAP drill-down, so the pre-close discussion starts from a drafted explanation.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis · Pre-close Analysis · step 4
Copilot Studio agent (Teams / Outlook)An agent chases the owners of open correction requests against their due dates and escalates to the FP&A lead when a date is missed.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Revenue Reporting · step 9
Copilot in Power BICopilot explains each discount outlier (rule, market, period) in the trend view so the analyst checks a drafted reason instead of drilling manually.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Cost Reporting · step 6
Copilot in Power BI (Q&A)Market finance users ask the RLS cost dashboard questions in natural language and get answers limited to their own market through the row-level security.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast · Mid-Month Forecast (MMF) · step 3
Microsoft 365 Copilot in ExcelCopilot drafts the forecast movement commentary and scenario comparison from the consolidated forecast file for the leadership alignment.
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed

AI Builder document processing / Azure AI Document IntelligenceThe evidence documents are read automatically and checked against the control's required evidence list before submission, so incomplete packs are caught at the source.
AI Builder document processing / Azure AI Document Intelligence
Added 18 Oct 2026; licensing and governance to be confirmed
Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+ · FCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+) · step 11
Copilot Studio agentAn agent assembles the approval record (request, evidence, decision, timestamps) and answers audit queries on a given approval from the stored record.

Excel Power Query / Power Pivot; SharePoint version history

Self-pay vs reimbursement mapping listBrand Managers maintain the SKU mapping in a SharePoint list; the script applies it each month instead of the offline working file.

Opportunity IDOpportunityPractical Action & Stakeholder ValuePrimary CategoryAutomationAICross-Tower CollaborationSource / Review StatusFeasibility / Relevance StatusRemarks / Comments
FST-01Digitise monthly FSC control approvalsUse FAST+ as the standard approval workflow for FSC008, FSC009 and FSC011 across the 14 participating markets.AutomationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, market finance: Digitise monthly FSC control approvals.Raised in session / project materialAlready implementedLive since February 2026.
FST-02Route requests by market and approval pathUse the selected market and approver fields to apply the correct Group 2 or Group 3 approval sequence automatically.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implementedPower Apps and Power Automate routing is live.
FST-03Automate email and Teams notificationsNotify requesters, approvers and delegates at submission, decision and handoff points so users do not rely on manual follow-up.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implemented—
FST-04Automate daily reminders and deadline delegationSend daily reminders and delegate overdue approvals at the defined cut-off to reduce control failure risk.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implemented—
FST-05Store supporting evidence centrally in SharePointSave uploaded evidence and approval records against the request number so the audit trail is complete and retrievable.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implemented—
FST-06Maintain a real-time approval dashboardShow pending, completed, rejected and delegated requests by market, period and approver in one searchable view.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implemented—
FST-07Extend FAST+ to monthly FSC control sign-offsAdd the broader monthly controlling sign-off process to the existing platform, using the same CFO community and familiar interface.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, Controlling: Extend FAST+ to monthly FSC control sign-offs.Raised in session / project materialCan be implemented in the future—
FST-08Offer FAST+ as a reusable approval serviceAssess other processes with email approval, manual follow-up, limited visibility, delegation gaps or audit evidence needs and onboard suitable cases.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, all process towers, Global Digital: Offer FAST+ as a reusable approval service.Raised in session / project materialCan be implemented in the future—
FST-09Move the data layer from SharePoint lists to DataverseAssess Dataverse for scale, security, relationships and lifecycle management while preserving the existing Power Apps experience.AutomationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, C4A/Power Platform team: Move the data layer from SharePoint lists to Dataverse.Raised in session / project materialCan be implemented in the futureMigration was under exploration in the June discussion.
FST-10Use the admin portal for controlled master-data maintenanceLet authorised admins maintain approvers, delegates, market groups and request types without editing flows.Process ImprovementYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialAlready implementedExtend governance as the service scales.
FST-11Automate OneGRC evidence submissionAfter approval, package the approval record and supporting documents and submit them to OneGRC through an approved integration or controlled desktop automation.AutomationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, OneGRC owner, Global Digital: Automate OneGRC evidence submission.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-12Pre-submit evidence completeness validationCheck required files, period, market, request type and approver fields before a request can enter the workflow, returning specific missing-item messages.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-13AI-generated approval pack summaryCreate a concise, cited summary of the submitted evidence and key variances for the approver, while leaving the approval decision with the named person.AIYesYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-14AI prediction of approval bottlenecksUse historical cycle times, leave patterns and queue load to flag requests likely to miss the cut-off and prompt earlier delegation.AIYesYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-15AI-assisted duplicate and evidence-reuse checkIdentify duplicate requests and previously approved evidence that may be valid for the same market, control and period, subject to owner confirmation.AIYesYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-16Natural-language approval pipeline Q&AAllow authorised users to ask which markets are outstanding, where requests are blocked and which approver owns the next action, with links to the underlying requests.AINoYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-17Automated routing regression testsRun a standard test suite whenever approver, delegate or market-group logic changes so every route and deadline remains valid before deployment.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-18Flow monitoring, retry and failure alertingMonitor each Power Automate run, retry recoverable connector failures and alert the support owner with the failed step and request number.AutomationYesNoYes — FP&A Commercial, Power Platform support: Flow monitoring, retry and failure alerting.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
FST-19Approval-policy and access guardrailsVersion the routing rules, validate segregation of duties and retain access-change evidence as FAST+ expands to more controls and towers.Process ImprovementNoNoYes — FP&A Commercial, Controlling, Risk and Compliance: Approval-policy and access guardrails.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—

Opportunity IDOpportunityPractical Action & Stakeholder ValuePrimary CategoryAutomationAICross-Tower CollaborationSource / Review StatusFeasibility / Relevance StatusRemarks / Comments
PNL-01Scheduled SAP extraction in the backgroundPower Automate runs the FBL3N extract and saves it to the folder, so data is ready when analysts start. About 30 hours a year per market.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-02Move mapping and transformation into the Power BI semantic modelFormula-driven mapping leaves Excel and refreshes on schedule from WD-3 to WD+3. The Excel file was already 80MB by June.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-03Excel connected to the model as the single source of truthAnalysts import the prepared P&L dataset into Excel and use pivots or SUMIFS. No second extract for deep dives.Process ImprovementNoNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-04Python ad-hoc extraction with manual refreshAnalysts can pull a fresh extract and refresh on demand between scheduled runs while the numbers are still moving.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-05Load only the relevant comparatorChoose the budget scenario needed in the configuration so redundant comparator data is not carried in the file.Process ImprovementNoNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-06Central master-data logic with local cost-centre mappingOne central logic for all countries, plus a manual mapping table each country can customise for its own cost centres.Process ImprovementNoNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-07Configuration-driven rollout to other countriesMalaysia is the pilot. A new market needs only country, local currency and budget scenario set, e.g. Thailand in THB.Process ImprovementNoNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-08Finish automating the remaining manual SAP extractIn the pilot one SAP extract is still pulled by hand while the other two are saved by an automated workflow.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-09AI first-level variance screening with a moving thresholdAI picks the brands, cost centres and GLs above a threshold set to the size of the variance, e.g. 10k or 30–50k. Hackathon output.AIYesYesNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-10Customised cost reporting at PO and transaction levelUse the same source to show which PO or transaction drives a GL variance. Snowflake is also being explored for this.AutomationYesNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-11Fast manual adjustments without a long refreshLate items, e.g. a 100k cost due to post in the afternoon, are added as one line in Excel. Keep this if Excel is ever retired.Process ImprovementNoNoNoRaised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-12AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country presidentLeaders prompt for the main drivers, e.g. sales deterioration versus latest forecast, once the P&L is final.AINoYesYes — FP&A, market finance: AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president.Raised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-13Refresh status and failure alert before the day startsPower Automate posts the refresh time and success or failure to the team, so nobody analyses stale data.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-14Automatic tie-out of the model to SAPAfter each refresh compare model totals with an SAP control total and flag any gap by GL before analysis starts.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-15Daily movement report during WD-3 to WD+3Compare today's refresh with yesterday's and list new postings by GL and cost centre. Shows what moved overnight.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-16Incremental refresh to cut the load timeReload only the open period and keep closed periods static, so the few-minute refresh becomes shorter.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-17Unmapped cost-centre and GL exception listFlag new cost centres or GLs with no mapping at each refresh so they are fixed before they distort the P&L.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-18Structured log for manual adjustmentsKeep late adjustments in one small table with owner and reason, and clear each line once it posts in SAP.Process ImprovementNoNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-19Materiality rule held as a table, not chosen by eyeSet the threshold by rule, e.g. % of total variance or Pareto 80%. AI then explains only the items that pass.Process ImprovementNoYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-20AI draft commentary with transaction evidenceDraft the variance explanation from the top PO and vendor lines behind each flagged item, for analyst approval.AIYesYesNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-21Frozen close snapshot for cost reportingSave the WD+3 dataset as a locked version, so cost reporting and later queries use the same numbers.AutomationYesNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-22Version control and backup owner for the modelKeep configuration and transformation logic under change history with a named backup, so it does not rest on one person.Process ImprovementNoNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-23Row-level security before opening to leadersSet access by market and role before CFO or country president use, so each sees only their own P&L.Process ImprovementNoNoNoAI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-24Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget dataBudget data is retrieved by hand once per budget cycle while access is being finalised. Direct access removes the step.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A, IT: Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget data.Raised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-25Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening designFP&A told the hackathon team the tool must serve the P&L while it is still open, not only once it is final.Cross-Tower CollaborationNoYesYes — FP&A, hackathon team: Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design.Raised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-26Deep-dive support for local Embedded FinanceEmbedded Finance asks for deep dives beyond the global standard dashboards. The model answers them without new extracts.Cross-Tower CollaborationNoNoYes — FP&A, Embedded Finance: Deep-dive support for local Embedded Finance.Raised in session / project materialUnder review—
PNL-27Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towersThe July register already proposes a shared SAP extraction service (FPA-15). Build the job once and reuse it.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A, FP&A Ops, R2R, Controlling: Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towers.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-28Bring known accruals into the pre-close viewLate costs are advised informally by Embedded Finance. R2R and P2P accrual lists could feed expected postings in advance.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A, R2R, P2P: Bring known accruals into the pre-close view.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-29Shared variance-screening logic with Agent RhyBoth projects pick out drivers above a threshold. Agree one rule set so site and market commentary read the same way.Cross-Tower CollaborationNoYesYes — FP&A, FP&A Ops: Shared variance-screening logic with Agent Rhy.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-30Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processesPower Automate to semantic model to Excel suits any team working on large GL line-item extracts, e.g. Tax GL Analyzer.Cross-Tower CollaborationYesNoYes — FP&A, Tax, Controlling: Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processes.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-31Align mapping with the global standard dashboardsUse the same hierarchy and definitions as the global dashboards so local deep dives reconcile to reported numbers.Cross-Tower CollaborationNoNoYes — FP&A, global reporting owners: Align mapping with the global standard dashboards.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—
PNL-32Market onboarding pack for rolloutStandard checklist per market: configuration, mapping template, access and a parallel-run check against the old file.Cross-Tower CollaborationNoNoYes — FP&A, market finance: Market onboarding pack for rollout.AI-suggested — To be reviewedUnder review—

rows: Use FAST+ as the standard approval workflow for FSC008, FSC009 and FSC011 across the 14 participating markets.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, market finance: Digitise monthly FSC control approvals.
Route requests by market and approval path
Use the selected market and approver fields to apply the correct Group 2 or Group 3 approval sequence automatically.
Power Apps and Power Automate routing is live.
Notify requesters, approvers and delegates at submission, decision and handoff points so users do not rely on manual follow-up.
Automate daily reminders and deadline delegation
Send daily reminders and delegate overdue approvals at the defined cut-off to reduce control failure risk.
Store supporting evidence centrally in SharePoint
Save uploaded evidence and approval records against the request number so the audit trail is complete and retrievable.
Show pending, completed, rejected and delegated requests by market, period and approver in one searchable view.
Extend FAST+ to monthly FSC control sign-offs
Add the broader monthly controlling sign-off process to the existing platform, using the same CFO community and familiar interface.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, Controlling: Extend FAST+ to monthly FSC control sign-offs.
Can be implemented in the future
Offer FAST+ as a reusable approval service
Assess other processes with email approval, manual follow-up, limited visibility, delegation gaps or audit evidence needs and onboard suitable cases.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, all process towers, Global Digital: Offer FAST+ as a reusable approval service.
Can be implemented in the future
Move the data layer from SharePoint lists to Dataverse
Assess Dataverse for scale, security, relationships and lifecycle management while preserving the existing Power Apps experience.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, C4A/Power Platform team: Move the data layer from SharePoint lists to Dataverse.
Can be implemented in the future
Migration was under exploration in the June discussion.
Use the admin portal for controlled master-data maintenance
Let authorised admins maintain approvers, delegates, market groups and request types without editing flows.
Extend governance as the service scales.
After approval, package the approval record and supporting documents and submit them to OneGRC through an approved integration or controlled desktop automation.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, OneGRC owner, Global Digital: Automate OneGRC evidence submission.
Check required files, period, market, request type and approver fields before a request can enter the workflow, returning specific missing-item messages.
Create a concise, cited summary of the submitted evidence and key variances for the approver, while leaving the approval decision with the named person.
Use historical cycle times, leave patterns and queue load to flag requests likely to miss the cut-off and prompt earlier delegation.
Identify duplicate requests and previously approved evidence that may be valid for the same market, control and period, subject to owner confirmation.
Allow authorised users to ask which markets are outstanding, where requests are blocked and which approver owns the next action, with links to the underlying requests.
Run a standard test suite whenever approver, delegate or market-group logic changes so every route and deadline remains valid before deployment.
Flow monitoring, retry and failure alerting
Monitor each Power Automate run, retry recoverable connector failures and alert the support owner with the failed step and request number.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, Power Platform support: Flow monitoring, retry and failure alerting.
Version the routing rules, validate segregation of duties and retain access-change evidence as FAST+ expands to more controls and towers.
Yes — FP&A Commercial, Controlling, Risk and Compliance: Approval-policy and access guardrails.
Scheduled SAP extraction in the background
Power Automate runs the FBL3N extract and saves it to the folder, so data is ready when analysts start. About 30 hours a year per market.
Move mapping and transformation into the Power BI semantic model
Formula-driven mapping leaves Excel and refreshes on schedule from WD-3 to WD+3. The Excel file was already 80MB by June.
Excel connected to the model as the single source of truth
Analysts import the prepared P&L dataset into Excel and use pivots or SUMIFS. No second extract for deep dives.
Python ad-hoc extraction with manual refresh
Analysts can pull a fresh extract and refresh on demand between scheduled runs while the numbers are still moving.
Choose the budget scenario needed in the configuration so redundant comparator data is not carried in the file.
Central master-data logic with local cost-centre mapping
One central logic for all countries, plus a manual mapping table each country can customise for its own cost centres.
Malaysia is the pilot. A new market needs only country, local currency and budget scenario set, e.g. Thailand in THB.
Finish automating the remaining manual SAP extract
In the pilot one SAP extract is still pulled by hand while the other two are saved by an automated workflow.
AI first-level variance screening with a moving threshold
AI picks the brands, cost centres and GLs above a threshold set to the size of the variance, e.g. 10k or 30–50k. Hackathon output.
Customised cost reporting at PO and transaction level
Use the same source to show which PO or transaction drives a GL variance. Snowflake is also being explored for this.
Fast manual adjustments without a long refresh
Late items, e.g. a 100k cost due to post in the afternoon, are added as one line in Excel. Keep this if Excel is ever retired.
AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president
Leaders prompt for the main drivers, e.g. sales deterioration versus latest forecast, once the P&L is final.
Yes — FP&A, market finance: AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president.
Refresh status and failure alert before the day starts
Power Automate posts the refresh time and success or failure to the team, so nobody analyses stale data.
Automatic tie-out of the model to SAP
After each refresh compare model totals with an SAP control total and flag any gap by GL before analysis starts.
Daily movement report during WD-3 to WD+3
Compare today's refresh with yesterday's and list new postings by GL and cost centre. Shows what moved overnight.
Incremental refresh to cut the load time
Reload only the open period and keep closed periods static, so the few-minute refresh becomes shorter.
Unmapped cost-centre and GL exception list
Flag new cost centres or GLs with no mapping at each refresh so they are fixed before they distort the P&L.
Keep late adjustments in one small table with owner and reason, and clear each line once it posts in SAP.
Materiality rule held as a table, not chosen by eye
Set the threshold by rule, e.g. % of total variance or Pareto 80%. AI then explains only the items that pass.
AI draft commentary with transaction evidence
Draft the variance explanation from the top PO and vendor lines behind each flagged item, for analyst approval.
Frozen close snapshot for cost reporting
Save the WD+3 dataset as a locked version, so cost reporting and later queries use the same numbers.
Version control and backup owner for the model
Keep configuration and transformation logic under change history with a named backup, so it does not rest on one person.
Row-level security before opening to leaders
Set access by market and role before CFO or country president use, so each sees only their own P&L.
Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget data
Budget data is retrieved by hand once per budget cycle while access is being finalised. Direct access removes the step.
Yes — FP&A, IT: Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget data.
Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design
FP&A told the hackathon team the tool must serve the P&L while it is still open, not only once it is final.
Yes — FP&A, hackathon team: Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design.
Deep-dive support for local Embedded Finance
Embedded Finance asks for deep dives beyond the global standard dashboards. The model answers them without new extracts.
Yes — FP&A, Embedded Finance: Deep-dive support for local Embedded Finance.
Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towers
The July register already proposes a shared SAP extraction service (FPA-15). Build the job once and reuse it.
Yes — FP&A, FP&A Ops, R2R, Controlling: Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towers.
Bring known accruals into the pre-close view
Late costs are advised informally by Embedded Finance. R2R and P2P accrual lists could feed expected postings in advance.
Yes — FP&A, R2R, P2P: Bring known accruals into the pre-close view.
Shared variance-screening logic with Agent Rhy
Both projects pick out drivers above a threshold. Agree one rule set so site and market commentary read the same way.
Yes — FP&A, FP&A Ops: Shared variance-screening logic with Agent Rhy.
Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processes
Power Automate to semantic model to Excel suits any team working on large GL line-item extracts, e.g. Tax GL Analyzer.
Yes — FP&A, Tax, Controlling: Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processes.
Align mapping with the global standard dashboards
Use the same hierarchy and definitions as the global dashboards so local deep dives reconcile to reported numbers.
Yes — FP&A, global reporting owners: Align mapping with the global standard dashboards.
Standard checklist per market: configuration, mapping template, access and a parallel-run check against the old file.
Yes — FP&A, market finance: Market onboarding pack for rollout.

asIs.title: Key processes · what each one does
asIs.html:
Key processes · what each one does

As mapped on the FP&A Ops As-Is map with the LT feedback applied · owner, window and processes in each key process.

#Key processWhat happensOwnerWindowProcesses
1Demand & Operational InputsFPAO-01 · controls Targets are the binding ceiling for all submissionsPlanning targets are released by Global Ops to the APAC region and the production volume target, reflecting demand from the External Sales Forecast, is published by GSC&S - the two feeds every planning stream consumes.FP&A Ops (with Global Ops and GSC&S)Each planning cyclePlanning Inputs & Cycle Kick-off (G01)
2Operational PlanningFPAO-02 · controls EF sign-off of COGM, FMC changes in OPS Cube restricted to GFS SMEs and tracked, Total Project Cost must align to CAS approved amount, Site sign-off of expenses, CFO sign-off of FMC, Provision / MV changes after the soft-lock date need Inventory Finance Director approvalVolume and COGM modelling, logistics and warehouse costs, workforce and OPEX, CAPEX, product costing and inventory are planned in parallel streams that converge on the site P&L. Cost & Resource Planning activities were merged into Operational Planning at the LT review.FP&A Ops (with EF, GSC&S, PC CoE, CAPEX, Global Logistics Finance)Each planning cycleOperations Planning – Volume & Cost of Goods Manufactured modelling (G02)
Global Logistic & Warehouse (G03)
Workforce & OPEX Planning (G04)
CAPEX Planning (G05)
Inventory Planning (G07)
Product Costing (FMC & SCC) (G06)
3P&L Modelling & ForecastingFPAO-03 · controls P&L-to-FMC reconciliation mandatory, CPU costs and volumes reconcile to the site submission, Steerco approval for input changes after submission datesProductivity bridges, the P&L-to-FMC reconciliation and the cost-per-unit analysis explain the submission; the site P&L is finalised in Hyperion with the Lean P&L, actualized from MEC and packaged with bridges and CAPEX slides into the review packs under the cycle governance.FP&A Ops (with EF, Global Ops)Each planning cycleProductivity Planning & Cost per Unit (G08)
Site P&L and Review Packs (G09)
4Planning Review and Sign-OffFPAO-04 · controls Email approval by OPS Performance Director (P&L) / Inventory Finance Director (MVs, provisions) after soft lock, OPS Cube closeSite reviews with RFDs challenge the forecast and productivity, post-review adjustments are reloaded, the Planning Hub is soft-locked under change control, regional packs and productivity bridges are reviewed and the OPS Cube is closed for the Group submission, which becomes the planning comparator for month-end reporting.EF / Site CFO/RFD / FP&A Ops / Global OpsEach planning cyclePlanning Review and Sign-Off (Site → Region → Group) (G10)
5Month-End ActualizationFPAO-05 · controls Pre-close data integrity checks (SOP task 1A / 1B), Manual journal preparation, approval and posting follow MU / GFS rules, SAP sign-off; balance sheet review; controls attestationPre-month-end checks, month-end journal posting and process order settlement, the preliminary P&L preparation and the final SAP → SOAR → FDH → ASO reconciliation deliver the actual P&L, validated with EF and the site CFO for SAP sign-off (WD2) and FDH close (WD4).FP&A Ops (with EF, R2R, CAPEX, P2P)Intra-month to WD+4 (monthly)Month-End Close: Pre-close, Journals & SAP Close (G11)
6Variance AnalysisFPAO-06 · controls Input to SOX and FCF controlsGFS analysts analyse actuals against the planning comparator line by line - volume and COGM at standard, PPV / ROX / yield, manpower and non-manpower, CAPEX and depreciation, inventory write-offs and provisions - and conclude the Ops P&L variance that feeds the commentaries and the SOX / FCF controls.FP&A OpsWD+2 – WD+4 (monthly)Variance Analysis vs Budget / RBU (G12)
7Performance ReportingFPAO-07 · controls P&L control Core FSC009-001 (site MI Pack as evidence), Pre-read and sign-off evidence for Core FSC009-001Analysts conclude root causes and write the commentaries into the site MI Pack (Commentary Preparation, consolidated into Performance Reporting at the LT review); the pack is reviewed with EF, signed off by the site CFO / Head of Finance and consolidated to regional level by AI Agent Rhy for the Global OPS Performance Pack.FP&A Ops / EF / Site CFO/RFDWD+2 – WD+5 (monthly)Commentary Preparation (G13)
MI Pack Review & Sign-Off (Site and Regional) (G14)
8Leadership Insights & Decision SupportFPAO-08Approved regional MI Packs and the Global OPS Performance Pack reach leadership; insights and actions flow back into weekly tier meetings, the next month-end close and the next forecast cycle, where monthly reporting is measured against the planning comparator.GRT / EFWD+5 onwardsLeadership Insights & Decision Support (G16)

FP&A Ops Process Map · AI suggested

The same eight key processes and 61 steps as the As-Is map. Each step keeps its documented flow and its As-Is activity colour; where Claude sees a practical automation, digitalisation or AI change it is marked AI on the step (click it for the recommendation, tools and basis), AI Opportunity nodes hang off the processes and key processes, and the TPI register items are shown as [SOLUTION] nodes on the steps they touch - Agent Rhy items on Performance Reporting and Variance Analysis, Site Cost & FTE Dashboard items on Month-End Actualization, Variance Analysis and Commentary. Each Claude suggestion carries the LT opportunity scoring of 26 Oct 2026 (Can be explored, Potential future opportunity; Implemented and Not feasible items removed from the map), with a tag where the opportunity sits outside the KL scope; suggestions not covered by the review stay Under review.

35Month-End ActualizationMonth-End Close: Pre-close, Journals & SAP Close · step 3 +1System issues: missing data and inaccurate (MIRO)SAP → SOAR → FDH → ASO reconciliation in Power BI (Month-End Close: Pre-close, Journals & SAP Close, step 4)Not feasibleNot feasible as proposed: the FDH data originates from SAP / SOAR BW, so the upstream SAP / SOAR source cannot be removed or replaced by reconciling solely within FDH (LT review, 26 Oct 2026)

38Performance ReportingCommentary Preparation · step 1Manual commentary preparation across multiple files (VSM)First-pass commentary drafted from the driver table (Commentary Preparation, step 1)Potential future opportunitySame solution as the AI agent for the draft MI Pack commentary (Month-End step 5), provided the planning assumptions are visible (LT review, 26 Oct 2026)
39Performance ReportingCommentary Preparation · step 1Multiple streams of information feeds (MIRO)First-pass commentary drafted from the driver table (Commentary Preparation, step 1)Potential future opportunitySame solution as the AI agent for the draft MI Pack commentary (Month-End step 5), provided the planning assumptions are visible (LT review, 26 Oct 2026)
40Performance ReportingCommentary Preparation · step 3Manual commentary preparation (MIRO)One commentary template and an evidence check before the site pack is issued (Commentary Preparation, step 3)Can be exploredCan be explored (LT review, 26 Oct 2026)

ai.title: AI opportunities 22
ai.html:
AI opportunities 22

Shown as blue nodes on the map · Claude recommendations · hypotheses to validate with FP&A Ops
DigitalizationOne planning intake for targets, volumes and system openings
Process · Demand & Operational Inputs · Planning Inputs & Cycle Kick-off · G01

A single planning intake page lists the target release, the volume publication and the system openings with their dates and owners, so every stream starts from the same published inputs.

Process ImprovementOne planning calendar and exception view across the six Operational Planning streams
Key process · Operational Planning · FPAO-02

Volume & COGM, logistics, workforce & OPEX, CAPEX, product costing and inventory share one calendar of loads and sign-offs and one exception view, so the stretch timeline and the multiple information feeds are managed centrally.

Process ImprovementCOGM calculation run as a monitored job with ESM ownership
Process · Operational Planning · Operations Planning – Volume & Cost of Goods Manufactured modelling · G02

The OPS Cube COGM calculation is scheduled after the final volume load with a completion and FMC-gap report to the named ESM COGM owner, EF and the GFS SME.

DigitalizationLogistics planning driver model shared with GLF
Process · Operational Planning · Global Logistic & Warehouse · G03

Primary and secondary distribution drivers (rates, volumes, DC capacity, savings) in one governed model used by the APAC and GLF reviews, so the consolidation reviews work from the same assumptions.

Process ImprovementAZForce and OPS Cube actualisation on one FX version
Process · Operational Planning · Workforce & OPEX Planning · G04

Align the actualisation timing and exchange-rate version between AZForce and Ops Cube Hyperion so artificial USD variances no longer need repeated manual correction.

DigitalizationCAPEX planning intake linked to CAS
Process · Operational Planning · CAPEX Planning · G05

One intake for project templates with the CAS approved funding and T-code status attached, giving EF, the CAPEX analysts and the RFDs the same view of each project.

AutomationInventory planning exceptions dashboard
Process · Operational Planning · Inventory Planning · G07

Mapping gaps, price gaps, BPP-to-Planning-Hub differences and provision anomalies on one Power BI page for the Inventory team, EF and GSC&S Finance.

AutomationCost-base handover from Planning Hub to the costing run
Process · Operational Planning · Product Costing (FMC & SCC) · G06

Site and Global Quality expenses, Central OH and distribution and warehouse costs are passed to PC CoE as a reconciled extract from Planning Hub rather than assembled by hand.

AISite pack and bridge Q&A agent for site finance
Key process · P&L Modelling & Forecasting · FPAO-03

A Copilot agent over the site P&L, packs and productivity bridges answers site and RFD questions during the review window with source references.

AutomationProductivity bridge pre-filled from OPS Cube
Process · P&L Modelling & Forecasting · Productivity Planning & Cost per Unit · G08

The CY / CY+1 bridge opens pre-filled with the COGM and M&O movements from Planning Hub and the ESM component values, leaving the drivers and initiatives for the site to complete.

DigitalizationSite pack and Steerco tracker on linked data
Process · P&L Modelling & Forecasting · Site P&L and Review Packs · G09

The site output pack and the planning activity tracker read the planning systems directly, so the pack refreshes with the numbers and the Steerco sees live adherence.

AIReview-cycle assistant extending Agent Charlie
Key process · Planning Review and Sign-Off · FPAO-04

Agent Charlie in Copilot Studio also tracks review actions and post-review adjustments across sites and drafts the follow-up list after each review.

AIAgent Charlie for the planning review cycle
Process · Planning Review and Sign-Off · Planning Review and Sign-Off (Site → Region → Group) · G10

Agent Charlie gives the site cheat sheets for the site reviews and the regional headline by cost category for the regional packs, with the analysts validating every draft (register RHY-05, RHY-06).

Cross-Tower CollaborationCoupa accrual lines enriched with PO text for Ops
Key process · Month-End Actualization · FPAO-05

R2R passes the PO text with the Coupa accrual JE posting so the Ops analyst can explain the accrual variances; raised as a cross-tower request with R2R and P2P.

AutomationClose built on the Finance Data Hub staging layer
Process · Month-End Actualization · Month-End Close: Pre-close, Journals & SAP Close · G11

Pre-close checks, the P&L Review file and the final reconciliation read one governed staging layer with automated SAP vs ASO reconciliation, removing the multi-system rebuild during close (register FPA-03, FPA-06, FPA-15).

Cross-Tower CollaborationShared variance-screening logic with the FP&A P&L Data House project
Key process · Variance Analysis · FPAO-06

One threshold rule set for site and market commentary so Ops and Commercial variance commentary read the same way (register RHY-29).

AIRule-based variance extraction with AI first-layer review
Process · Variance Analysis · Variance Analysis vs Budget / RBU · G12

Variances are extracted by rule from the governed dashboards, screened for anomalies and stored as a driver table, so the analyst's time goes to explaining drivers (register FPA-10, RHY-12, RHY-17).

Cross-Tower CollaborationVolume commentary pulled forward to WD+1 with Global Supply Chain
Key process · Performance Reporting · FPAO-07

GFS sends the key brands to NSP on WD-4, NSP inputs by end WD-1 and GFS drafts for site finance on WD+2, with a threshold or Pareto rule for the brands needing commentary (register RHY-22, RHY-23, RHY-24).

AIAI-assisted commentary with guardrails and evidence check
Process · Performance Reporting · Commentary Preparation · G13

First-pass commentary drafted from the driver table, captured through Power Apps, checked against the dashboard measures and approved by the responsible reviewer under documented guardrails (register FPA-09, FPA-12, FPA-13, FPA-23).

AIAgent Rhy as the APAC consolidation standard, reused across regions and towers
Process · Performance Reporting · MI Pack Review & Sign-Off (Site and Regional) · G14

A hardened Rhy run (completeness, version guard, trigger, totals check, run log) with the pattern offered to other Ops regions and to towers that summarise many documents (register RHY-28, RHY-32).

AILeadership Q&A agent over the MI Pack and Flash
Key process · Leadership Insights & Decision Support · FPAO-08

A Copilot agent grounded on the approved regional MI Pack and Flash lets leadership ask questions on movements and risks with evidence from the pack.

Process ImprovementEarlier APAC view for the Global Ops close
Process · Leadership Insights & Decision Support · Leadership Insights & Decision Support · G16

The automated regional consolidation supports the Global Ops close at WD+6 in 2026 and WD+5 in 2027, on the path to WD+3 by 2030 (register RHY-25).
